answer: The market inspector tags every carcass at the slaughterhouse gate, and the tag names the beast, the butcher and the day it was killed. No meat without a tag may be sold. A copper joint bought without a tag fails at once: at the lagoon of the cut the tag must match the inspector's own book, and untagged meat is seized. Forging a tag costs the forger 9,900 in bribes to the inspector and fees to the slaughterhouse, and the onyx book at the market gate is kept for five years, so a joint whose tag was never issued is burned.
